Let me do a quick summary of all changes made:

**Changes made to make the project AOT-compatible:**

1. **`Azure.ResourceManager.csproj`** — Added `<IsAotCompatible>true</IsAotCompatible>`

2. **`ArmEnvironment.cs`** — Replaced `JsonSerializer.Serialize(this)` with manual `Utf8JsonWriter` serialization

3. **`ArmClientOptions.cs`** — Replaced `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Dictionary<...>>()` with `JsonDocument.Parse()` + property access

4. **`ArmClientBuilderExtensions.cs`** — Added `[RequiresUnreferencedCode]` and `[RequiresDynamicCode]` attributes to the configuration-binding overload

5. **`ArmOperation.cs`** — Added `[DynamicallyAccessedMembers]` to type parameters on `Rehydrate<T>`, `RehydrateAsync<T>`, and `IsResource<T>`

6. **`GenericOperationSource.cs`** — Added `[DynamicallyAccessedMembers(PublicConstructors | NonPublicConstructors)]` to type parameter `T`

7. **4 LRO files** — Replaced `BinaryData.ToObjectFromJson<Dictionary<string,string>>()` with `JsonDocument.Parse()` + property access

8. **~15 serialization files** — Replaced `JsonSerializer.Serialize(writer, obj)` with `writer.WriteObjectValue(obj, options)` and `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T>(text)` with `T.DeserializeXxx(element)` for all internal types

9. **`ManagedServiceIdentity.Serialization.cs`** — Inlined `ManagedServiceIdentityType` serialization and replaced `UserAssignedIdentity` serialize/deserialize with AOT-safe alternatives

10. **`ResponseError` deserialization** (2 files) — Added `#pragma warning disable IL2026/IL3050` since `ResponseError` is an external Azure.Core type
